newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission says EU cereal prices too high.
newsitem.headline: Commission says EU cereal prices too high.

text.p: Cereal prices in the European Union are too high, a European Commission official told Reuters on Tuesday.
"The high internal price is inexplicable. There is going to be a good harvest but farmers don't appear to have got the message," the official said.

Officials believe that farmers are holding back stocks despite this year's EU harvest -- variously estimated in the region of 200 million tonnes. One official said, "They don't need to sell because they are cash-rich from too high direct payments which are coming on stream."
COCERAL, the European grain traders umbrella group, confirmed that Commission officials told delegates to the cereals advisory committee on Friday that prices must come down.

"They said that prices were too high and they were especially critical of the restitution level for barley. At 31 Ecus per tonne they said that four times the amount of wheat could be exported for the price," a COCERAL official said.

Other trade sources said that prices in Austria are highest at 25 percent above the intervention price and between 10 and 15 percent above intervention price in Germany and France. Only in the United Kingdom and Finland are prices close to intervention.

One source said, "This week's cereals management committee is likely to be interesting. The Commission is expected to announce measures to force down domestic prices, most likely by rejecting or limiting export refunds."
